title: LinkedIn Professional Network: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable LinkedIn-style professional networking platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a scalable LinkedIn-style professional networking platform. The system must support user profiles with work history, education, and skills; connection requests and acceptance with degree-of-connection rules; a feed of posts, articles, and job updates; job posting and search with applicant tracking; skill endorsements and recommendations; direct messaging; company pages; and online learning courses. The platform must efficiently traverse the professional graph to suggest connections and jobs while maintaining profile privacy controls.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Users can create rich profiles with work experience, education, skills, and certifications
Users can send, accept, or ignore connection requests with 1st/2nd/3rd degree visibility rules
Users can view a personalized feed of posts, articles, and job updates from their network
Users can create text, image, or article posts and engage with likes, comments, and reposts
Recruiters can post jobs with descriptions, requirements, and application questions
Job seekers can search jobs by title, company, location, and experience level
Users can endorse skills and write recommendations for their connections
Users can send and receive one-on-one messages with read receipts
Companies can create pages with updates, job openings, and employee counts
Users can take online learning courses with video lectures and completion certificates

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Profile pages must load in under 300ms including connections and endorsements
Job search must return relevant results in under 500ms across millions of postings
Feed generation must handle users with thousands of connections efficiently
Graph traversal for 'People You May Know' must complete in under 1 second
99.9% availability for profile views, messaging, and job applications
Privacy controls must enforce who can view profile sections based on connection degree
Learning platform must support video streaming with adaptive bitrate

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application where profiles, connections, feed, jobs, messaging, and learning share a single deployment and database. This validates the professional graph and privacy requirements before introducing the complexity of distributed graph services.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for profile photos and media
  - Azure SignalR Service or AWS AppSync for real-time messaging
  - Single database with tables for Users, Profiles, Connections, Posts, Jobs, Messages, Endorsements

data.text: As the professional graph grows into hundreds of millions of users, split the monolith into microservices optimized for profile reads, graph traversal, feed generation, job matching, and real-time messaging. The Profile Service is the source of truth for user identity.

items: User Service: Manages user identity, authentication, and profile metadata. Acts as the source of truth for user IDs, names, emails, and privacy settings. Other services call this service to resolve user identity.
Profile Service: Handles rich profile data including work history, education, skills, and certifications. Supports privacy-aware queries so only authorized viewers see full profile details.

Connection Service: Manages the professional graph—send/accept/reject connection requests, query 1st/2nd/3rd degree connections, and compute mutual connections. Uses a graph database or adjacency-list storage for efficient traversal.

Feed Service: Generates personalized feeds from posts, articles, and job updates in the user's network. Uses a push model for users under 5,000 connections and a pull model for users with larger networks.

Job Service: Handles job posting, search, and application tracking. Indexes jobs with filters for title, company, location, and experience level. Stores applications and tracks applicant status through the hiring pipeline.
Messaging Service: Enables one-on-one and group conversations with real-time delivery via WebSocket. Stores message history and enforces privacy so only connected users can message each other.
Notification Service: Delivers alerts for connection requests, post interactions, job alerts, and messages. Supports in-app, email, and push notification channels with user preference controls.
Recommendation Service: Suggests 'People You May Know' using graph algorithms (common connections, shared companies/schools) and recommends jobs based on profile signals and application history.

data.title: React App Structure
data.code:
src/
  features/
    linkedin/
      profile/            # Profile page with rich sections and privacy controls
      my-network/         # Connection list, requests, and degree indicators
      feed/               # News feed with posts, articles, and job updates
      jobs/               # Job search, listings, and application tracker
      messaging/          # Conversation list and chat with real-time updates
      notifications/      # Notification center with tabs and preferences
      companies/          # Company pages with updates and employee info
      learning/           # Course catalog with video player and progress tracking
      api/                # API clients per service
      components/         # Shared UI components
      hooks/              # Custom hooks
      store/              # Zustand/Jotai state
      types/              # TypeScript interfaces
  shared/
    ui/                  # Design system
    lib/                  # Utilities
    hooks/                # Global hooks

Key Patterns:
  - Privacy-aware rendering that hides profile sections based on viewer relationship
  - Infinite scroll feed with cursor-based pagination
  - Optimistic connection requests with rollback on failure
  - Real-time messaging via WebSocket with message queue for offline delivery
  - React Query for caching profile data with background refetch
  - Intersection Observer for lazy-loading job cards and course thumbnails

data.title: Connection Service (ASP.NET Core)

cards.title: Compute
cards.description: Run profile, feed, job, and messaging API servers
pros: Auto-scaling for peak job-search and networking activity
cons: Graph-intensive workloads may need GPU instances

cards.title: API Gateway
cards.description: Rate limit and route profile, job, and messaging requests
pros: Edge caching for popular company pages and job listings
WAF protection against scraping and fake profiles
cons: Additional cost for high-volume API calls

cards.title: Cache
cards.description: Cache profiles, feed posts, and job search results
pros: Sub-millisecond profile loads for active users
cons: Cache invalidation for frequently updated profiles

cards.title: Database
cards.description: Store profiles, connections, jobs, and applications
pros: Strong ACID guarantees for job applications and connections
Global replication for low-latency profile access
cons: Graph traversal is slow without a dedicated graph engine

cards.title: Storage
cards.description: Store profile photos, resume documents, and course videos
pros: Cheap, durable storage for millions of profile photos
CDN delivers media with low latency globally
cons: Video transcoding pipeline adds processing latency

cards.title: Messaging
cards.description: Async events for connections, posts, and job applications
pros: Decouples messaging from profile and connection services
Buffers notification spikes during viral posts
cons: Message ordering is not guaranteed across partitions

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Professional networks are graph-heavy; efficient connection traversal is the core algorithmic challenge
Privacy and degree-of-connection rules must be enforced consistently across all services
Feed generation is asymmetric: users with few connections use fan-out, while influencers use pull-based timelines
Job search benefits from inverted indexing and machine learning ranking based on profile fit
Start with a monolith on Azure SQL or AWS RDS, then extract Connection, Feed, and Job as the first microservices
data.takeaway: LinkedIn Professional Network is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
